evidence.summary: With the other inputs held constant, increasing post_length from 26.5 to 100 increased the observed score from 0.9411 to 0.9897. Intermediate values were 0.9695 at 50 and 0.9865 at 85.5.

Holding the numeric inputs constant, surface produced the largest observed score variation: A=0.9872, B=0.9876, C=0.0560, and D=0.9900. Surface C therefore produced a 0.9340 lower score than D in this controlled comparison.
With the other inputs held constant, increasing recent_strikes from 0 to 2 reduced the score from 0.9897 to 0.9822, and 2.5 reduced it further to 0.9792.
With other inputs held constant, increasing reputation from 300 to 320, 510, and 900 reduced the observed score from 0.9898 to 0.9883, 0.9672, and 0.9277 respectively.
With the other inputs held constant, increasing reach from 1 to 10, 51, and 97.5 reduced the score from 0.9889 to 0.9874, 0.9746, and 0.9205.
With other inputs held constant, increasing months_active from 0 to 1 produced a small score decrease from 0.9900 to 0.9897.
In the controlled account-age comparison, increasing account_age_days from 65 to 75 increased the observed score from 0.9882 to 0.9898.
Changing linked_accounts from 0 to 10 to 20 produced the same observed score of 0.9900 in these controlled queries, so no measurable effect was observed in this region.
Changing mentions from 6 to 0 to 3 produced the same observed score of 0.9900 in these controlled queries, so no measurable effect was observed in this region.
Changing report_ratio among 1, 0, and 0.5 produced an observed score of 0.9900 in all three controlled queries, so no measurable effect was observed in this region.
